newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr ends higher, market short before govt news.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr ends higher, market short before govt news.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed higher on Monday in a short market ahead of the expected announcement of a new government on Tuesday.
A late spurt pushed the kiwi to US$0.7061/68 and 67.12 on its Trade-Weighted Index, up from 0.7026/33 and 66.82 at the opening.

Nothing market-moving emerged from intensive last-minute meetings before Tuesday's expected announcement by nationalist New Zealand First of its choice of coalition partner between the conservative National and centre-left Labour parties.

Maverick National MP John Banks, adamantly opposed to trading away planned tax cuts, said he was pleased with progress at a meeting of the party's MPs. Labour meanwhile was seeking a pledge of support from the left-wing Alliance.
"It's been short for a few days waiting for this announcement, and each day we don't get an announcement it seems to drift a little bit higher with the stop-losses," an Auckland dealer said.
He expected some selling around 0.7070/75, with a possible drift back to the 45/50 area.

The market favours a National-led coalition but would look hard at concessions offered to NZ First under such an arrangement, especially on tax cuts, spending and a possible widening of the Reserve Bank's inflation target.

"If National are prepared to make a lot of changes to their policy then I'd see us heading lower over the next few days," a dealer said. Labour and NZ First have both consistently demanded a lower kiwi dollar, and the currency could be expected to react accordingly if the two form a government.
NZ First MPs are due to meet on Tuesday to make their choice. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
